To better understand and reduce PIH, we aim to locate model components responsible for PIH. Prior work has shown that attention heads often serve specific functional roles, such as information copying Olsson et al. ( 2022 ); Feucht et al. ( 2025 ) and context tracking Prakash et al. ( 2025 ) , whereas MLP layers are more closely associated with storing parametric knowledge Meng et al. ( 2023 ); Arad et al. ( 2024 ) . Therefore, we focus our analysis on identifying attention heads associated with PIH. To analyze the causal role of individual attention heads in PIH, we perform attention head knockouts using mean ablation ( Wang et al. ( 2022 ); Mueller et al. ( 2025 ) , see Appendix ˜ D for technical details). Intuitively, this intervention removes token-specific information carried by the head while preserving its overall activation magnitude. We apply this procedure head-by-head and quantify knockout success as the fraction of samples that switch from the prompted count to the true count under the misaligned prompt. We rank heads by success and select the top- m m heads per model.
